summary: Flag-driven scene data traversal and update. Depending on the a2/a3 flag bits: zeroes this+0x1B0 when a2 has bit 0x20, ORs this+0xEC with 0x800 when a3 has bit 0x20, walks the node list at this+0x100 (and the node at this+0x108) invoking RecursiveTraversal, propagates 0x40/0x80/0xC0 flag bits through a chain reached via this+0x110, then processes up to four (count, pointer-array) pairs at this+0x1B4..0x1D0 clearing per-element flag/fields selected by the a3 0x1800 mask. Called by sub_4FA7E0.

operations.description: When a2 has bit 0x20 set, zero the DWORD at this+0x1B0 (this[108]).
Otherwise, when the low byte of a3 has bit 0x20 set, OR the DWORD at this+0xEC (this[59]) with 0x800.
Walk the node list whose head is this+0x100 (this[64]); for each node (next link stored at node+0x104) whose DWORD at node+0xEC is non-zero, call RecursiveTraversal(a2, a3, 0).
If the node pointer at this+0x108 (this[66]) is non-null, call RecursiveTraversal(a2, a3, 0) on it.

Follow the chain rooted at (*(this+0x110) + 36); while a node is non-null, set or clear flag bits 0x40, 0x80 or 0xC0 at node+0x9C according to the a2 & 0x1800 and a3 & 0x1800 masks (0x40 for 0x800, 0x80 for 0x1000, 0xC0 for 0x1800), advancing via the link stored at node+0xC0.

For each of the four (count, pointer-array) pairs at this+0x1B4/0x1B8, this+0x1BC/0x1C0, this+0x1C4/0x1C8 and this+0x1CC/0x1D0 (this[109..116]): when the count is positive, iterate that many elements of the array using a 132-byte stride.

Per element, dispatch on the a3 & 0x1800 mask (jump table at global 0x545F24): for 0x800 clear the element's 0x400 flag; for 0x1000 walk 8 sub-slots (stride 16 DWORDs) zeroing slot fields when the first sub-slot DWORD equals 8; for 0x1800 do both.
Return the last processed element count.

clean_pseudocode: case 0x1000: clear 8 sub-slots whose value == 8; break;
unresolved: The deterministic facts attribute the 0x9C/0xC0 flag-chain to base *(this+0x134) (fields *(this+0x134):0x9C and *(*(this+0x134)+0xC0):0xC0, plus this+0x134), while the Hex-Rays rendering roots it at *(this+0x110)+36; the two bases cannot be reconciled from this packet alone.
The node-list fields are likewise attributed to base *(this+0x204) (offsets 0xEC and 0x104) by the facts, whereas the source renders them relative to the list node; base mismatch unresolved.

Guard on field this+0x1F4 == 8 and the RW fields this+0x1F4, this+0x1F8, this+0x200 are present in the facts but have no visible operation in the raw source text; their role is unproven (possibly an element/version gate for the clearing loop).
Owner class and the concrete meaning of the a2/a3 flag masks (0x20, 0x1800) are unconfirmed.
